newsitem.title: USA: Northeast fire injures two workers in Conn.
newsitem.headline: Northeast fire injures two workers in Conn.

text.p: NEW LONDON, Conn., Aug 19 (Tuesday) - An explosion and fire at a dormant electrical substation Tuesday injured two Northeast Utilities workers, a utility spokesman said.
The two workers, whose names were not released, received first- and second-degree burns on their chests and faces, Northeast spokesman Bruno Ranniello said.
The injuries were not life-threatening, he said.
The injured workers were being treated at Bridgeport Hospital Burn Center, but their condition was not immediately known.
The company is conducting a probe to determine the cause of the explosion at the Hempstead Street Substation, Ranniello said.
The workers were in the early stages of dismantling the station, which no longer serves customers and is being replaced by a larger station, he said.
"They were operating equipment in the station, and during the process, an explosion and fire on one of the switches occurred," Ranniello said.
"The switch that exploded caused a short circuit, which knocked out power to eight customers in New London for a brief period."
Power was restored within an hour, he said.
Ranniello said the damage to the substation was not extensive, and that the fire was well-contained in the small building.
